prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "dalleserver", with the standing line "An HTTP server that turns an Ethereum address into a prompt set and one annotated image, cached and locked." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A single left-to-right path drawn as a working line. At left, a browser request arrives as a labelled URL slip carrying a series name and a long hexadecimal address. It passes through two gates: a series check against the known series list, and an address check counting characters. Past the gates, a padlock keyed to the pair of series and address; one request opens it and runs, a second concurrent request is turned aside and joins a waiting queue that only watches. Beyond the lock, eight linked stages drawn as a chain of small trays, each feeding the next: setup, base prompts, enhance prompt, image prep, image wait, image download, annotate, completed. A short curved return path leaves the enhance stage and rejoins the chain, showing that a failed enhancement falls back to the unenhanced prompt. Above the chain, a bypass arc labelled cache hit leaps from the gates directly to the finished image when a file already exists on disk.

Magnified circles set beside it show circle one, the per-pair padlock with its expiry timer, showing that a stale lock releases itself. circle two, the breaker with three positions, closed, open, half-open, and the counters that move it. circle three, a file written first as a temporary file then renamed into place, showing no half-written file is ever visible.

Colour is used so that Warm orange marks the live generation path and anything that costs an outside call. Cool blue marks the cached and read-only path, including files already on disk. Grey-green marks failure handling, retries, fallback, and skip mode. Everything else stays neutral.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: eight stages from setup to completed; five prompt texts written per address; five failures open the breaker; three attempts per enhancement; five-minute lock; 42 characters in the address.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: series and address name the two path segments at the gates. generate sits on the arrow that starts work. lock-ttl sits on the padlock timer. data, title, terse, prompt, enhanced sit on the five text files. annotated sits on the finished image. cache hit sits on the bypass arc. percent, eta seconds and done sit on the polled progress reply.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: /dalle/<series>/<address>, ?generate=1, series check, 42-character address, generation lock, base prompts, enhance prompt, image wait, image download, annotate --lock-ttl, breaker opens, three attempts, temp then rename /series, /preview, /metrics, health check data, title, terse, prompt, enhanced, annotated image, gallery page percent, eta seconds, cache hit, done, skip image mode

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Second request waits, never duplicates work; Missing key runs the whole path unimaged. Lock expires so a crash cannot block; Enhancement failure returns the original prompt. Gallery lists finished images newest first; Health reports the breaker state. Five prompt texts, one image, per address; Removing the image keeps the prompts. Poll the same address until done.
